# The Five Plot Engines {#sec-tech-engines}

Each engine is a `app/view/visualization_<kind>.R` module plus one or two
`app/logic` modules that do the computing and drawing. This chapter collects the
implementation notes for all five; the coordinator that mounts them is
@sec-tech-visualization.

## Minimum spanning tree {#sec-tech-engines-mst}

The split is strict: `phylo.R` computes the graph on **Generate**; `mst_plot.R`
turns that graph into a `visNetwork` [@visnetwork] on every control change.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-tech-mst
%%| fig-cap: "MST pipeline. Everything above the line runs once per Generate; everything below redraws on control changes."
flowchart TD
  subgraph COMPUTE["app/logic/phylo.R — on Generate"]
    P["allele profiles (mlst + staged)"] --> D["Hamming distance matrix"]
    D --> Z["collapse zero-distance isolates<br/>(igraph components)"]
    Z --> G["igraph mst()"]
  end
  subgraph DRAW["app/logic/mst_plot.R — on control change"]
    G --> L["mst_layout(): fixed coordinates"]
    L --> E["mst_edge_lengths()"]
    E --> CL["mst_clusters() + blobs"]
    CL --> N["node sizes · pies · labels"]
    N --> V["visNetwork (visualization_mst.R)"]
  end
```

### Building the graph {#sec-tech-engines-mst-compute}

`compute_mst()` reads the profiles, applies the chosen NA policy, and builds the
graph — but first it **collapses zero-distance isolates**, transitively:

```{.r filename="app/logic/phylo.R"}
# Collapse zero-distance samples into groups (transitive: chained identical
# profiles merge into one node).
zero_adj <- prep$dist == 0
membership <- components(
  graph_from_adjacency_matrix(zero_adj, mode = "undirected", diag = FALSE)
)$membership
...
graph <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(rep_dist, mode = "undirected",
                                     weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
tree  <- mst(graph)
```

The result is an `igraph` MST [@igraph] whose vertices carry a `name` (the
newline-joined member isolates) and `n` (the member count). `phylo.R` stops here,
on purpose — everything about *drawing* is the other half.

### The four load-bearing drawing decisions {#sec-tech-engines-mst-draw}

`app/logic/mst_plot.R` owns geometry, colour, clustering and legend. Its header
names four decisions that each replace a vis.js default that produced a *wrong*
rendering, not merely a plain one:

::: {.callout-important title="1 — Coordinates are computed on the server, not by browser physics"}
Node positions come from `mst_layout()`, not from vis.js's force simulation. A
Barnes-Hut simulation over a few hundred nodes was both the slowest part of the
render (it re-stabilised from scratch on every control change — the reload lag) and
the *least faithful*: springs treat allelic distance as a preference that repulsion
overrules, so the drawn distance between two isolates was not their distance. Fixed
coordinates with physics off is simultaneously the performance fix, the fidelity
fix, and the fix for the previous densely tangled rendering under "Skeleton" mode.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="2 — Edge length is an explicit transform of allelic distance"}
`mst_edge_lengths()` maps allele distance to pixels through a named transform
(`mst_length_mode()`), so the median edge is a fixed length and proportional
lengths are used only while the longest edge stays within a legible ratio — a graph
with one 3000-allele outlier does not compress everything else into a single point.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="3 — Clustering uses the scheme's own published threshold"}
`mst_clusters()` groups nodes within a distance **threshold**, defaulting to the
scheme's published cluster distance where it has one (`mst_threshold_default()`
reads it from `scheme_overview`). That default is what makes the number in the
"cluster at" control comparable to standard cluster nomenclatures (e.g. EnteroBase
HierCC). Clusters can be drawn as blobs (`mst_cluster_blobs()`) or contracted
(`mst_collapse()` — a contraction of a tree is still a tree).
:::

::: {.callout-important title="4 — A node is a set of isolates"}
Because zero-distance isolates merge, a node represents *several* isolates, and the
drawing respects that: `mst_node_radii()` sizes a node by area proportional to its
count (radius ∝ √count); `mst_node_values()` turns a categorical variable over the
node's members into a **pie**, the one channel that can show all of them rather
than collapsing to one; `mst_node_labels()` shows a few members then "+N more";
`mst_node_titles()` builds the hover tooltip; `mst_gradient_colors()` handles a
continuous variable.
:::

`app/view/visualization_mst.R` owns the `visNetwork` render, the control panel and
all MST-specific reactive state, and exports via the **widget** route
(@sec-tech-viz-export).

## Phylogenetic trees {#sec-tech-engines-tree}

`compute_phylo_tree()` prepares the distances (needing at least three isolates) and
`build_tree()` runs one of two classic algorithms via `ape` [@ape]:

```{.r filename="app/logic/phylo.R"}
build_tree <- function(dist_mat, labels, algo) {
  d <- as.dist(dist_mat)
  tree <- if (identical(algo, "UPGMA")) {
    as.phylo(hclust(d, method = "average"))         # UPGMA
  } else {
    nj_tree <- nj(d)                                # Neighbour-Joining
    nj_tree[["edge.length"]] <- pmax(nj_tree[["edge.length"]], 0)
    nj_tree
  }
  tree$tip.label <- labels
  tree
}
```

::: {.callout-important title="Branch lengths stay in allele units; negatives are clamped, not rescaled"}
Branch lengths are left in the raw units of the distance matrix (allele
differences), the same units the MST labels its edges in — a pair shown "3272
apart" is reported identically in both views. NJ's least-squares fit can produce a
slightly negative branch, which has no biological meaning, so those are clamped to
zero — the standard fix other NJ viewers apply — rather than compressed. Rescaling
here would silently desynchronise the tree from the MST.
:::

`app/logic/tree_plot.R` paints the tree as a `ggtree`/`ggplot` object
[@yu2017ggtree] so control changes re-render cheaply. Most of it is layout
arithmetic:

- `tree_auto_layout()` derives aspect ratio, font sizes and element scaling from
  the number of tips.
- `tree_axis_breaks()` / `tree_axis_layer()` draw a ticked axis to the *same scale
  as the branches*.
- `tree_branch_keep()` decides, from the drawn geometry, which branches are wide
  enough to legibly carry a printed length — a *rendering* decision, deliberately
  separate from what a branch length means.
- `tree_inward_xlim()` supports the inward-circular layout.
- `tile_total()`, `heatmap_panels()`, `heatmap_header_frac()` lay out tile strips
  and heatmap panels in register with the tips; `tree_legend_ncol()`,
  `tree_legend_width_in()`, `tree_branch_format()`, `tree_branch_digits()` handle
  legend and label formatting.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-tech-tree
%%| fig-cap: "Tree pipeline: one compute (NJ/UPGMA) feeds many cheap ggtree renders with auto layout and metadata annotation."
flowchart LR
  D["distance matrix<br/>(phylo.R)"] --> B["build_tree()<br/>NJ or UPGMA"]
  B --> A["tree_auto_layout()"]
  A --> R["ggtree render<br/>(tree_plot.R)"]
  M["metadata + custom vars"] --> MAP["mapping_engine<br/>(tip colour/shape/tiles)"]
  MAP --> R
  R --> P["visualization_tree.R"]
```

`app/view/visualization_tree.R` carries the NJ/UPGMA picker and exports via the
**ggplot** route.

## Epidemic curve {#sec-tech-engines-epi}

The epi engine computes no pairwise distances: it bins the metadata's collection
dates straight into counts. Binning is cheap (a `group_by` over the metadata), so
once a curve exists every control re-bins live rather than waiting for Generate. It
takes local isolates only and ignores NA handling.

```{.r filename="app/logic/epi_plot.R"}
#' Parses dates, constructs composite stratifications, and calculates case
#' [counts per interval].
build_epi_data <- function(...) { ... }
```

`epi_default_interval()` picks the finest interval whose bar count stays under a
cap; `floor_date_bin()` snaps each date to its interval (ISO-8601 weeks starting
Monday). Unparseable dates return `NA` and are dropped with a reported count.

::: {.callout-important title="Integer breaks and one-interval-wide bars are load-bearing"}
Counts are whole cases, so the y-axis carries only **integer breaks**, and every bar
is exactly **one interval wide** so a gap in the curve is a genuine gap in the data
rather than a drawing artefact. These are not cosmetic defaults — changing either
makes the reader misread the shape of the outbreak.
:::

Derived series: `epi_cumulate()` (running total) and `epi_moving_average()` (fills
temporal gaps with zero, then a rolling mean; `epi_moving_avg_label()` names it).
Stratification is `epi_stratum()`; palettes are constrained by
`epi_scale_choices()` and interpolated by `epi_fit_scale()` / `epi_palette()` so a
12-group stratification never silently drops groups to grey. Annotations are
lane-packed so labels do not collide.

Playback is driven by the view's own tick loop — each step rebuilds the curve with
the reveal cut one interval further on — rather than `gganimate`, so it needs no
special renderer.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-tech-epi
%%| fig-cap: "The epi curve bins dates into counts; derived series and strata layer on cheaply, so controls re-bin live."
flowchart LR
  MD["metadata dates<br/>(+ stratify var)"] --> B["build_epi_data()<br/>floor_date_bin · counts"]
  B --> C["epi_cumulate()"]
  B --> MA["epi_moving_average()"]
  B --> R["ggplot render<br/>(visualization_epi.R)"]
  C --> R
  MA --> R
```

`app/view/visualization_epi.R` renders the `ggplot` through `renderImage` (via
`ggsave`, so the whole frame takes the theme background) and exports via the
**ggplot** route.

## Map {#sec-tech-engines-map}

Isolate locations come from the metadata's spatial fields — `geo_loc_name_city`,
`geo_loc_name_state_province`, `geo_loc_name_country`. `app/view/visualization_map.R`
geocodes each **distinct** place once, on Generate, via OpenStreetMap / Nominatim —
not once per isolate, which would be hundreds of identical calls against a
rate-limited public service.

Four modes share a single builder (`build_map`), so they stay visually consistent
and the same builder backs the HTML export:

| Mode | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Markers** | Styled points, one cluster per location |
| **Choropleth** | Countries shaded by isolate count (Natural Earth polygons) |
| **Heatmap** | Point-density surface |
| **Charts** | A mini-chart per location (`leaflet.minicharts`) |

Rendering is a single `renderLeaflet` reacting to the geocoded coordinates and a
**debounced** bundle of all control inputs, so dragging a slider does not re-geocode
or thrash the map. Labels for arbitrary and imported columns come from
`app/logic/field_labels.R`; country polygons come from `rnaturalearth`. Export is
the **widget** route.

## AMR heatmaps {#sec-tech-engines-amr}

Like the map and epi curve, this engine computes no pairwise distances and takes
local isolates only — a staged peer's imported profile carries allele identity and
nothing else (@sec-tech-interop-staging).

`app/view/visualization_amr.R` offers three views:

| View | Source | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| **Gene heatmap** | `amr_results` | isolates × genes presence/absence |
| **Drug-class matrix** | `amr_summary` | isolates × drug class, call confidence |
| **Prevalence bars** | either | most prevalent genes or classes |

::: {.callout-important title="A partial call is never shown as a confident one"}
The drug-class matrix preserves abritamr's `section` distinction: a confident
**match** and a **partial** call are coloured differently, and when duplicate hits
land in one cell the highest-confidence rank takes precedence (`amr_class_matrix()`,
`.section_rank()`). Collapsing the distinction would overstate an isolate's
resistance.
:::

`app/logic/amr_plot.R` does the database reads and matrix construction, keeping the
view module thin and the pure parts unit-testable (@sec-testing):

```{.r filename="app/logic/amr_plot.R"}
#' Attaches gene metadata attributes to support heatmap annotations.
amr_presence_matrix <- function(...) { ... }   # isolates x genes (0/1)
#' Takes the highest confidence rank when duplicate hits exist per cell.
amr_class_matrix    <- function(...) { ... }   # isolates x drug class
#' Returns top `top_n` items ordered by prevalence.
amr_prevalence      <- function(...) { ... }
```

Genes can be grouped by element type (AMR / VIRULENCE / STRESS) or drug class, or
clustered (`amr_gene_meta()`, `amr_gene_choices()`, `.column_layout()` with an
optional dendrogram). Rows and columns carry annotations for the grouping and for
any mapped variable (`.row_annotation()`, `.class_annotation()`), with
category-safe palettes shared with the epi engine (`amr_palette()` ≡
`epi_palette()`).

The heatmaps are built with `ComplexHeatmap` and converted to a `ggplot`
(`build_amr_heatmap()`, `build_amr_class_heatmap()`, `amr_as_ggplot()`); the
prevalence view is a native `ggplot` bar chart (`build_amr_prevalence()`). Export
is therefore the **ggplot** route.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-tech-amr-hm
%%| fig-cap: "The AMR engine reshapes the two screen tables into three ggplot views."
flowchart LR
  R[("amr_results")] --> PM["amr_presence_matrix()"]
  S[("amr_summary")] --> CM["amr_class_matrix()"]
  R --> PV["amr_prevalence()"]
  S --> PV
  PM --> H1["gene heatmap"]
  CM --> H2["drug-class matrix"]
  PV --> H3["prevalence bars"]
```

## Chapter summary

- MST: `phylo.R` computes (distance matrix → zero-distance collapse → `igraph`
  MST), `mst_plot.R` draws (server coordinates, explicit edge-length transform,
  scheme-threshold clustering, set-valued nodes).
- Tree: `build_tree()` runs NJ or UPGMA on the same matrix, branch lengths in
  allele units with NJ negatives clamped; `tree_plot.R` does the layout arithmetic.
- Epi: date binning only, integer axes, one-interval bars; playback is a tick loop.
- Map: geocode per distinct place on Generate, four modes through one `build_map`,
  debounced render.
- AMR: two tables reshaped into three views, preserving the match/partial
  distinction.
